a & b is 0110 & 0011 = 0010 = 2, so flag = (2 > 1) = true; 'C' has ASCII 
value 67 = 0100_0011, and & 0x0F masks to the lower 4 bits giving 0000_0011 = 3; 
since flag is true the ternary picks a ^ b = 0110 ^ 0011 = 0101 = 5; finally  
3 | 5 = 0011 | 0101 = 0111 = 7. The main traps are forgetting that char has an ASCII 
value that can be used in bitwise ops, and that & 0x0F is a common masking trick to grab the 
lower nibble.
